title: Area of Triangles
contentObjective: I can find the area of a triangle using the formula A = ½ × base × height.
languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words base, height, area, and perpendicular.

noticeAndWonder.context: This floor is tiled with squares, and each square is split into triangles of different wood tones.
wonderStarters: I wonder what would happen if…

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Painting a Cabin
revealWordProblem.text: The front of this A-frame cabin is a triangle with a base of 34 ft and a height of 23¾ ft. Find the area of the triangular front that needs to be painted.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 34 × 23¾. First, 23¾ = 23.75, so 34 × 23.75 = 807.5. Then take half: 807.5 ÷ 2 = 403.75. The triangular front of the cabin has an area of 403.75 square feet.

turnAndTalk.question: At the build site you survey a triangular garden bed with a base of 12 feet and a height of 8 feet. Which measurement is the height, and how is it different from the slanted side?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The height is the perpendicular distance from the base to the top corner.

stems.en: The height is the ___ distance from the base to the top corner.
stems.es: La altura es la distancia ___ desde la base hasta la esquina de arriba.

stems.en: It is different from the slanted side because ___.
stems.es: Es diferente del lado inclinado porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students identify the height as the perpendicular (straight-up, 90-degree) distance from the base to the opposite vertex, not the slanted side.
turnAndTalk.extend: Does it matter which side of the triangular panel you call the base? Justify your thinking using the formula A = 1/2 x b x h.
extendStems: It ___ matter which side is the base because ___.
No matter which base I choose, the area is the same since ___.

turnAndTalk.question: Your triangular panel (base 12, height 8) fits inside a 12 by 8 rectangle. Why do we divide by 2 to find the triangle's area before cutting the glass?
turnAndTalk.kernel: A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height.

stems.en: A triangle is half of a ___ with the same base and height.
stems.es: Un triángulo es la mitad de un ___ con la misma base y altura.

stems.en: So the area is 1/2 times 12 times 8, which equals ___.
stems.es: Entonces el área es 1/2 por 12 por 8, que es ___.

stems.en: The rectangle's area is ___, so the triangle is ___.
stems.es: El área del rectángulo es ___, entonces el triángulo es ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: A strong answer states the triangle is half of the 12 x 8 = 96 rectangle, so the panel area is 48 sq ft, and connects the 1/2 to that halving.
turnAndTalk.extend: Two glass panels both have area 48 sq ft. Must they have the same base and height? Justify or give a counterexample.
extendStems: They ___ have the same base and height because ___.
A counterexample is a triangle with base ___ and height ___, which also gives ___.

turnAndTalk.question: At the client review, the homeowner paints a triangular A-frame wall with base 20 ft and height 14 ft; one can covers 50 sq ft. Talk through how many cans the budget needs.
turnAndTalk.kernel: Find the triangle area first, then divide by what one can covers.

stems.en: The wall's area is 1/2 times 20 times 14, which equals ___ square feet.
stems.es: El área de la pared es 1/2 por 20 por 14, que es ___ pies cuadrados.

stems.en: She needs ___ cans because ___ divided by 50 equals ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students compute area = 140 sq ft, then 140 / 50 = 2.8, and reason she must round up to 3 cans to cover the whole wall.
turnAndTalk.extend: Why can't the budget order exactly 2.8 cans? Explain what rounding up means in this real situation and how it changes the leftover paint.
extendStems: She must round up to ___ cans because ___.
The leftover paint covers about ___ sq ft, since ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice on Area of Triangles, what strategy did you use when a problem felt tricky?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height. A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height.

stems.en: A triangle is half of a ___ with the same base and height.
stems.es: Un triángulo es la mitad de un ___ con la misma base y altura.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming a specific strategy tied to 6.GR.1 — not just "I multiplied." They should connect steps to the key idea.
turnAndTalk.extend: How would you help a classmate who made the common mistake from today's lesson? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

mission.title: The Triangular Skylight
mission.story: You are the lead architect at Sky Harbor Studio. The city has hired your firm to design a glass skylight made of triangular panels for the new transit hub. Before the glass can be cut, you must master the area of triangles — every wrong measurement wastes expensive glass.
mission.objective: Calculate the area of triangular panels accurately so the skylight fits perfectly.

scenes.name: Model Workshop
scenes.text: Plot the triangular garden bed on the blueprint grid and see how it fits inside its 12 × 8 rectangle — the triangle is exactly half.

scenes.name: Panel Calculations

visual.caption: The triangular garden bed sits inside a 12 ft by 12 ft grid, filling a 12-by-8 rectangle. What do you notice about how much of that rectangle the triangle covers -- and what do you wonder about the two empty corners?

launch.narrative: Your architecture firm is designing a park with triangular garden beds. The client wants to know exactly how much soil to order, which means calculating the area of each triangular section. The first garden has a base of 12 feet and a height of 8 feet.
launch.contextImage: Architectural blueprint with triangular garden sections marked in green

What measurements do we need to find the area?
How is the area of a triangle related to the area of a rectangle?

conceptIntro.heading: How do we find the area of a triangle?
conceptIntro.intro: A triangle has three sides. The base is one side, and the height is the straight-up (perpendicular) distance from the base to the top corner.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height. A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My triangular garden has a base of 12 feet and a height of 8 feet.
I write the formula: A = ½ × base × height.
I put in the numbers: A = ½ × 12 × 8.
I take half: ½ × 96 = 48. So the area is 48 square feet.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now a smaller triangle: base = 10 cm, height = 6 cm.
Now take half: what is ½ × 60? Yes, 30.
So the area is 30 square centimeters.

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: Next you will plot the triangle on a grid and see how it fits inside a rectangle.
Remember: multiply base × height, then take half.

explore.instructions: Plot the vertices of a triangle with base 12 and height 8.
explore.label: Plot the three vertices of the triangular garden bed.

discourse.prompt: The triangle fits inside a 12 × 8 rectangle. How does the triangle's area compare to the rectangle's area?
discourse.sentenceFrame: The area of the triangle is ___ the rectangle because A = 1/2 × ___ × ___ = ___ square feet.

approaching.stem: What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm?
approaching.scaffold: Use A = ½ × b × h. First multiply base × height, then take half.
approaching.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 square centimeters.
choiceFeedback: Add 5 + 9, divide result by 2, then × 4.
The bases are the parallel sides.
Follow A = (b₁ + b₂) ÷ 2 × h exactly.
hints: A triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm — remember a triangle is half of a matching rectangle.
The matching rectangle would be 10 × 6. Your triangle covers only half of that space.
Compute 10 × 6, then divide the product by 2. Answer in square centimeters.

approaching.stem: A triangle has an area of 24 sq ft and a base of 8 ft. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: Add the bases: 6 + 8 = 14.
Divide by 2, then multiply by 5.
Do not forget any step.
hints: The area (24 sq ft) and base (8 ft) are known — the height is the mystery number.
Since half of the base 8 is 4, every foot of height adds 4 sq ft of area.
Ask: 4 times what height equals 24? Divide 24 by 4 to find out.

approaching.stem: What is the area of a triangle with base 14 ft and height 6 ft?
choiceFeedback: Which two sides are parallel?
The height is perpendicular to them.
Identify bases and height correctly.
hints: Base 14 ft, height 6 ft — and the shape is a triangle, not a rectangle.
One easy path: take half of the base first (½ × 14 = 7), then multiply by the height.
Multiply 7 × 6 and label the result in sq ft.

approaching.stem: A triangular window pane has a base of 9 in and a height of 4 in. What is its area?
approaching.scaffold: Use A = ½ × b × h. Multiply 9 × 4 first, then take half.
choiceFeedback: Exactly ONE pair of parallel sides is a trapezoid.
TWO pairs would be a parallelogram.
Count the parallel pairs.
hints: The pane's base is 9 in and its height is 4 in — triangle rules apply here.
You can halve either number first. Half of the height 4 is 2, which makes the multiplication easy.
Compute 9 × 2 (that's ½ × 9 × 4 rearranged) and give your answer in square inches.

approaching.stem: Which formula gives the area of a triangle with base b and height h?
approaching.scaffold: A triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height. Which formula shows 'half'?
approaching.explanation: A triangle covers exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height, so A = ½ × b × h.
choiceFeedback: That's the rectangle's area — a triangle is half of it.
Area multiplies base and height, it doesn't add them.
You doubled instead of halving — a triangle uses ½, not 2.
hints: Picture cutting a rectangle along its diagonal — each piece is a triangle.
Rectangle area is b × h. Decide whether a triangle needs more, less, or the same — and by what factor.
Two identical triangles fill one b × h rectangle, so look for the formula that takes a fraction of b × h.

approaching.title: Spot Marcus's Mistake

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Find the area of a triangle with base 9 ft and height 5 ft.

approaching.correctWork: Marcus added the base and height instead of multiplying. Area is the space inside the shape, not a sum of the side lengths. The correct formula is A = ½ × b × h: A = ½ × 9 × 5 = ½ × 45 = 22.5 square feet.
hints: Adding 9 + 5 measures a length, not the space inside the triangle — area needs multiplication, not addition.
Use A = ½ × base × height: multiply 9 × 5 first, then take half. ½ × 45 = 22.5 sq ft.

onLevel.hint: Use A = (b1 + b2) / 2 x h; work backwards for missing values.
hints: Gardens A and D are missing area; Gardens B and C are missing a base or height — those need backwards steps.
Missing area: ½ × b × h. Missing base or height: double the area first, then divide by the measurement you know.
Garden B: double 27 to get 54, then divide 54 by the base 9 to find the height.

onLevel.label: Match each shape to its area.
onLevel.hint: Calculate each area using the trapezoid formula, then compare.
hints: Three cards are triangles and one is a rectangle — they don't share the same formula.
Triangles: multiply base × height, then halve. The rectangle: just multiply 7 × 3.
Start with 'Triangle b=8, h=6': take half of 8 × 6. Match it, then work the other triangles.

onLevel.title: Find Dana's Mistake

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Find the area of a triangle with base 10 ft and height 7 ft.

onLevel.correctWork: Dana forgot the ½. The area is half of base × height: A = ½ × 10 × 7 = ½ × 70 = 35 square feet.
hints: Look at the multiply step — did Dana use every part of the formula A = ½ × b × h?
The ½ is missing. A triangle is only half of the rectangle, so you must take half of 70.

onLevel.stem: A triangular sail has an area of 30 sq m and a height of 12 m. What is its base?
choiceFeedback: Work backward: 30 = ½ × b × 12, so 30 = 6 × b.
That looks like 30 − 12 — undo the area formula instead.
You multiplied — divide to undo ½ × base × height.
hints: The area (30 sq m) and height (12 m) are known — the base is what you're solving for.
Simplify ½ × 12 = 6 first, so the equation reads 30 = 6 × b.
Divide 30 by 6 to find the base in meters.

extending.prompt: An architect designs a triangular roof gable with a base of 18 ft and a height of 9 ft. A second gable has the same area but a base of 27 ft. Find the area of the first gable, then determine the height of the second gable. Show all your work.
extending.sentenceFrame: The first gable's area is ___ sq ft because A = ½ × ___ × ___. The second gable has the same area, so ___ = ½ × 27 × h, which means its height is ___ ft.
hints: Two things to find: the first gable's area from base 18 and height 9, then the second gable's height.
Step 1: A = ½ × 18 × 9. Step 2: set that same area equal to ½ × 27 × h and solve backwards.
Compute ½ × 18 × 9 first. Then, since ½ × 27 = 13.5, divide the area by 13.5 to get the new height.

extending.stem: A composite logo is made of a rectangle (8 cm by 6 cm) with a triangle on top. The triangle has a base of 8 cm and a height of 5 cm. What is the total area of the logo?
extending.explanation: Rectangle: 8 × 6 = 48 sq cm. Triangle: ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 sq cm. Total: 48 + 20 = 68 sq cm.
choiceFeedback: That's only the rectangle — add the triangle's area too.
You used full base × height for the triangle — it needs ½.
Recheck the triangle: ½ × 8 × 5, then add the rectangle.
hints: The logo has two parts: a rectangle (8 cm by 6 cm) and a triangle on top (base 8 cm, height 5 cm).
Find each part with its own formula, then combine — the triangle needs the ½, the rectangle doesn't.
Compute 8 × 6 for the rectangle and ½ × 8 × 5 for the triangle, then add the two areas.

extending.prompt: A rectangle is 12 ft by 8 ft. A diagonal line cuts it into two triangles. What is the area of each triangle? Explain how the triangle area formula relates to the rectangle area formula.
extending.sentenceFrame: The rectangle's area is ___ because ___. Each triangle's area is ___ because a diagonal splits a rectangle into ___ equal triangles.
extending.hint: Plot the four vertices; use A = (b1 + b2) / 2 x h.
hints: Start with the rectangle: its area comes from 12 × 8. The diagonal splits it into two identical triangles.
Each triangle keeps the same base (12) and height (8) as the rectangle — so its area is half the rectangle's.
Compute 12 × 8, halve it for one triangle, then check with ½ × 12 × 8. Explain why both paths agree.

optional.stem: What is the area of a triangle with base 16 m and height 5 m?
choiceFeedback: One pair of parallel sides = trapezoid.
Does this have one or two pairs?
Check which sides actually match up parallel.

optional.stem: A triangle has an area of 36 sq cm and a height of 9 cm. What is its base?
choiceFeedback: A trapezoid has TWO parallel bases.
Add both bases in the formula.
The height is perpendicular between the bases.

optional.stem: Two triangles have the same area. One has a base of 12 ft and a height of 6 ft. The other has a base of 9 ft. What is the height of the second triangle?
optional.explanation: First area = ½ × 12 × 6 = 36 sq ft. Then 36 = ½ × 9 × h → 36 = 4.5h → h = 8 ft.
choiceFeedback: Add the two bases: (b₁ + b₂).
Divide by 2, then multiply by height.
Formula: A = (b₁ + b₂) ÷ 2 × h.

optional.stem: You design a triangular roof gable for a client's cabin. The base measures 8 ft and the height measures 5 ft. What is the area of the gable?
optional.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 8 × 5 = ½ × 40 = 20 square feet.
choiceFeedback: That's base × height — a triangle's area is half of that.
You added base and height — multiply and take half instead.
Correct value, but area needs square feet.

optional.stem: A triangle flag has base 12 in and height 7 in (the slanted sides are 10 in). Find its area.
optional.explanation: Use the perpendicular height (7 in), not a slanted side. A = ½ × 12 × 7 = ½ × 84 = 42 square inches.
choiceFeedback: Use the perpendicular height (7), not the slant side (10).
You used the slant side — area uses the perpendicular height.
That's base × slant — use ½ × base × perpendicular height.

optional.stem: Your studio designs a triangular road sign with a base of 6 ft and a height of 9 ft. What is its area?
choiceFeedback: That's base × height — take half for a triangle.
You added instead of multiplying — use ½ × 6 × 9.
Right number — but area is in square feet.

optional.instructions: On your blueprint, sort each segment of the triangular sign into the correct column: the perpendicular height you use in the formula, or a side you do NOT use as the height.

items.text: A dashed line from the top corner straight down to the base at a 90° angle
The perpendicular distance from the base up to the opposite vertex
A slanted side that leans from the base up to the top corner
The longest slanted edge of the triangle

optional.label: Match each triangular design's base and height to its correct area.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension: Gallery Walk — Check the Designer's Flag

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: A triangular flag has a base of 10 ft. Its slanted side is 8 ft, and the perpendicular height marked by a dashed line is 6 ft. Find the area.

optional.correctWork: The designer used the 8 ft slanted side instead of the perpendicular height. The formula needs the height that meets the base at a 90° angle, which is 6 ft. A = ½ × 10 × 6 = ½ × 60 = 30 square feet.
hints: Look at the substitute step. Which number did the designer plug in for the height — the slanted side or the perpendicular dashed line?
The height must meet the base at a 90° angle. That is the 6 ft dashed line, not the 8 ft slanted side. Recompute with h = 6.

optionalActivity.name: Triangle Design Studio
optionalActivity.intro: Step up to the drafting table and design signs, roofs, and flags by calculating the area of each triangular piece with A = ½ × base × height.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Area of Triangles is stopping after multiplying base × height and forgetting to take half — for example, computing 12 × 8 = 96 and writing 96 sq ft instead of 48 sq ft. Another common mistake is using a slanted side as the height instead of the perpendicular (straight-up) distance from the base. Before you submit, ask: Did I take half of base × height? Is my height measurement perpendicular to the base?

exitTicket.stem: A triangle has a base of 11 inches and a height of 8 inches. What is its area?
choiceFeedback: That's base × height — remember the ½ for a triangle.
You added instead of multiplying — use ½ × base × height.
Right number, wrong unit — area is square inches.
hints: Base 11 inches, height 8 inches — and it's a triangle, so there's one extra step after multiplying.
Use A = ½ × b × h. Multiplying without the ½ gives the rectangle's area, which is double the triangle's.
Find 11 × 8, then take half of the product. Label it in square inches.
